Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 43 (Digital Realty missing-address campaign): added an address from a listing dedicated to this exact building code.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, Digital Realty IAD43, Building S, matches a Baxtel listing dedicated to this exact building code, giving 44820 Prentice Drive, Ashburn, VA.

profile.facility_type_note: Part of Digital Realty's Northern Virginia (Ashburn/Loudoun/Sterling/Reston/Bristow/Fairfax) data center campus, one of the largest concentrations of colocation buildings in Data Center Alley. Digital Realty publishes individual building pages with real street addresses for most named buildings in this campus (for example IAD37 at 44060 Digital Loudoun Plaza Bldg K, IAD36 at 43780 Digital Loudoun Plaza Bldg H, IAD40 at 44372 Round Table Plaza Bldg M, VA4 at 8217 Linton Hall Road in Bristow, VA3 at 1780 Business Center Drive in Reston), confirmed via digitalrealty.com and third-party colocation marketplaces (UPSTACK, datacenterHawk).

reading.body:
Digital Realty IAD43 Building S sits within the operator's Northern Virginia campus, a multi-building cluster in the Ashburn-Loudoun area that collectively represents one of the largest concentrations of colocation infrastructure in the United States. The operator publishes approximately 600 MW of IT load across this entire regional campus as of 2023, but does not publish a building-specific capacity figure for IAD43 itself, so the size of this individual facility cannot be determined from available data.

Virginia ranks 24th nationally by published data center capacity, with 1,375 MW confirmed across all operators with disclosed figures. The state has 326 mapped facilities but only 23 with published megawatt figures, meaning most capacity in Virginia remains undisclosed. Digital Realty's Northern Virginia footprint is substantial enough to rank among the state's largest concentrations, though individual building capacities within the campus are not separately disclosed.

This facility qualifies as a colocation data center with standard enterprise-grade infrastructure. Its relevance to AI scaling depends on the undisclosed power and density within this specific building and on whether its power supply can expand to meet accelerator demand, neither of which can be determined from the published specifications.
